# Research Note: The 2026 Browser AI Platform — What Changed and What It Means for EdgeInfer

*Auto-generated by the R&D research loop (#3), August 2026. All claims cited to live sources.*

## Headline platform shifts (2026)

### 1. WebGPU is Baseline
As of January 2026, WebGPU ships stable in Chrome/Edge (113+), Safari 26+ (macOS Tahoe, iOS, iPadOS, visionOS), and Firefox 141+ on Windows / 145+ on macOS ARM64. Linux Firefox and older iPhones remain on WebGL2 fallback ([utsubo.com frontier APIs 2026](https://www.utsubo.com/blog/frontier-web-apis-2026-production-ready), cross-checkable on [caniuse](https://caniuse.com/webgpu)).

**Implication for EdgeInfer:** the WebGPU→WASM fallback ladder is no longer a hedge against "Chrome-only" — it now mostly covers *older hardware* (pre-A12 iPhones, Linux Firefox, budget Android), not whole browsers. The README's Known Limitations line about "Firefox without flag" is outdated as of Firefox 141+ on Windows/macOS and should be re-checked per release.

Caveat that still applies: shader compilation is asynchronous with a cold-start cost (1–5 s reported for ONNX WebGPU pipelines; first-frame compile can exceed 200 ms even for simple pipelines). Pipeline caching/warm-up matters more than provider choice for perceived latency.

### 2. WebTransport went Baseline in March 2026
Safari 26.4 shipped WebTransport unflagged in March 2026, joining Chrome (since M97), Edge, and Firefox (since 114) — ([utsubo.com](https://www.utsubo.com/blog/frontier-web-apis-2026-production-ready); [testmuai.com browser-support guide](https://www.testmuai.com/learning-hub/webtransport-browser-support/)). Reported latency-jitter advantage over WebSocket on lossy mobile networks: 30–50% for low-latency streaming workloads.

**Relevance to the zero-server cluster:** model-bundle delivery and sync of inference results across peers no longer needs a WebSocket shim; HTTP/3 server prerequisites are CDN-dependent. Not an EdgeInfer code change today, but it belongs in any architecture note connecting EdgeInfer to peervault/meshauth.

### 3. ONNX Runtime Web 1.29: native WebGPU EP becomes the destination
Microsoft released ONNX Runtime **1.29 on 12 Aug 2026**, expanding native WebGPU support, adding Arm64 CPU kernels, and announcing **deprecation of the WebGL and JSEP browser paths** in favor of the native WebGPU execution provider ([curiouslm.com analysis](https://curiouslm.com/blog/onnx-runtime-1-29-webgpu-local-ai); release notes at [onnxruntime.ai](https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/tutorials/web/ep-webgpu.html)).

**Concrete EdgeInfer action items:**
- The README's `>= 1.21.0` guidance predates this. When EdgeInfer bumps its dependency, verify: session configuration, operator coverage on the native WebGPU EP (quantized attention variants and fused kernels are known gaps), and console operator-fallback warnings (they indicate silent CPU execution).
- `RuntimeManager.detectCapabilities()` should eventually distinguish `webgpu-native` vs legacy JSEP so users can tell which path they're actually on.
- Deprecation ≠ removal: keep testing the WASM path explicitly; it remains the compatibility floor.

### 4. Backend decision data: WebGPU vs WASM is task-shaped, not uniform
A reproducible benchmark methodology (Feb 2026) found ([sitepoint.com](https://www.sitepoint.com/webgpu-vs-webasm-transformers-js/)):
- Small single-pass tasks (embeddings, classification, short inputs): **WASM wins or ties** — all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding in ~8–12 ms on M2 via WASM+SIMD vs 15–25 ms WebGPU (dispatch overhead dominates).
- Autoregressive generation ≥100 M params: **WebGPU wins 10–15×** — TinyLlama-1.1B at 25–40 tok/s on discrete GPU vs 2–5 tok/s WASM.
- INT8 quantization benefits WASM 2–3× over FP32 (SIMD-friendly); WebGPU prefers FP16, with INT8/INT4 op coverage varying by GPU/driver.
- Batched image inference strongly favors WebGPU.

**Implication for EdgeInfer's API:** a static "is WebGPU available → use WebGPU" heuristic is wrong for the embedding/classification workloads EdgeInfer targets. A `backendHint(taskShape)` style helper (or documented decision matrix in the README) would encode this: WASM default for small single-pass models, WebGPU for generation/batched workloads, WASM-only when cold-start or broad-device compatibility dominates.

Note: EdgeInfer's own historical benchmark numbers were correctly removed from the README as unverifiable; the numbers above are third-party and hardware-specific, offered here only as external reference points, not EdgeInfer claims.

### 5. Local-first context: OPFS complete, sync engines mainstream
OPFS (Origin Private File System) now has full cross-browser support, giving web apps a real local file layer for cached model weights ([buildmvpfast.com local-first survey](https://buildmvpfast.com/blog/local-first-software-saas-rxdb-pouchdb-sync-2026)). The CRDT/sync-engine ecosystem matured through 2025–2026 (Yjs, Automerge 3, Loro, Zero, ElectricSQL; surveys: [youngju.dev deep-dive](https://youngju.dev/blog/culture/2026-05-15-crdt-local-first-engines-2026-yjs-automerge-loro-replicache-liveblocks-deep-dive.en), [local-first landscape](https://emne.com/e/curator/the-local-first-software-landscape-whats-actually-shipping-in-2026)). Two still-hard problems noted there: unbounded CRDT metadata growth ("The Long Now") and composing E2EE with merge logic.

**Fit for EdgeInfer + peers:** ModelCache over OPFS + meshauth identities + a sync engine covers five-plus of Ink & Switch's seven local-first ideals; the E2EE-composition problem is exactly what Preeo's encrypted on-device approach and meshauth's design grapple with. Worth a dedicated architecture note later.

### 6. WebNN: not yet
Chrome origin-trials WebNN in M147–M149 (Android excluded); Safari/Firefox have not shipped ([utsubo.com](https://www.utsubo.com/blog/frontier-web-apis-2026-production-ready)). EdgeInfer's `hasWebNN` capability flag stays forward-looking; NPU access via web standard remains a 2027 story.

## Summary table

| Capability | Status Aug 2026 | EdgeInfer relevance |
|---|---|---|
| WebGPU | Baseline since Jan 2026 | Fallback ladder now covers old hardware, not old browsers |
| Native WebGPU EP (ORT) | Recommended path; WebGL/JSEP deprecated in ORT 1.29 (Aug 2026) | Bump dep + expose native-vs-JSEP in detectCapabilities |
| WASM SIMD | Universal, best for small/single-pass models | Default backend for embeddings/classification |
| WebTransport | Baseline since Mar 2026 (Safari 26.4) | Transport option for cluster sync; needs HTTP/3 CDN |
| OPFS | Full cross-browser support | ModelCache persistence target |
| WebNN | Chrome origin trial only | Keep hasWebNN flag aspirational |
